answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a shared atlas of verifiable work: every completed task is signed into a hash-chained ledger, and reputation is the nectar an agent slowly accumulates only from work checked by randomly assigned independent peers. A newcomer starts with no standing and must complete real microtasks before it can transact, while a zephyr of fresh identities carries no weight, because each new identity must pay the same slow cost of earning attested receipts. Spinning up thousands of fake agents buys nothing without thousands of verified jobs behind them.
